metadata.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Double Q-learning
metadata.authors: Hado van Hasselt, Arthur Guez, David Silver

nodes.name: Action value $Q_\pi(s,a)$ under policy $\pi$
nodes.statement: For policy $\pi$, the value of action $a$ in state $s$ is $Q_\pi(s,a) \equiv \mathbb{E}[R_1 + \gamma R_2 + \ldots \mid S_0=s, A_0=a, \pi]$, with discount $\gamma \in [0,1]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected discounted return when taking action a in state s and following policy pi thereafter.

nodes.name: Optimal action value $Q_*(s,a)$
nodes.statement: $Q_*(s,a) = \max_\pi Q_\pi(s,a)$. An optimal policy is obtained by selecting the highest-valued action in each state.

nodes.name: Parameterized value function $Q(s,a;\boldsymbol{\theta})$
nodes.statement: A parameterized approximation $Q(s,a;\boldsymbol{\theta}_t)$ to action values, used when state space is too large to tabulate.

nodes.name: Deep Q-Network (DQN)
nodes.statement: A multi-layer neural network mapping state $s \in \mathbb{R}^n$ to a vector of action values $Q(s,\cdot;\boldsymbol{\theta}) \in \mathbb{R}^m$ with parameters $\boldsymbol{\theta}$.

nodes.name: Target network $\boldsymbol{\theta}^-$
nodes.statement: A second network with parameters $\boldsymbol{\theta}^-$ that copies the online network every $\tau$ steps and is held fixed in between, used to compute the bootstrap target.

nodes.name: Experience replay
nodes.statement: Observed transitions are stored in a memory bank and sampled uniformly to update the network, decorrelating updates.

nodes.name: Q-learning parameter update
nodes.statement: $\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t+1} = \boldsymbol{\theta}_t + \alpha (Y^{Q}_t - Q(S_t,A_t;\boldsymbol{\theta}_t)) \nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}_t} Q(S_t,A_t;\boldsymbol{\theta}_t)$.

nodes.name: Q-learning target $Y^{Q}_t$
nodes.statement: $Y^{Q}_t \equiv R_{t+1} + \gamma \max_a Q(S_{t+1}, a; \boldsymbol{\theta}_t)$.

nodes.name: DQN target $Y^{DQN}_t$
nodes.statement: $Y^{DQN}_t \equiv R_{t+1} + \gamma \max_a Q(S_{t+1}, a; \boldsymbol{\theta}^-_t)$, using the target network for evaluation.

nodes.name: Q-learning target rewritten with selection/evaluation split
nodes.statement: $Y^{Q}_t = R_{t+1} + \gamma Q(S_{t+1}, \arg\max_a Q(S_{t+1}, a; \boldsymbol{\theta}_t); \boldsymbol{\theta}_t)$ — the same weights $\boldsymbol{\theta}_t$ select and evaluate.

nodes.name: Double Q-learning target $Y^{DoubleQ}_t$
nodes.statement: $Y^{DoubleQ}_t \equiv R_{t+1} + \gamma Q(S_{t+1}, \arg\max_a Q(S_{t+1}, a; \boldsymbol{\theta}_t); \boldsymbol{\theta}'_t)$ — online weights $\boldsymbol{\theta}_t$ select, second weights $\boldsymbol{\theta}'_t$ evaluate.

nodes.name: Double DQN target $Y^{DoubleDQN}_t$
nodes.statement: $Y^{DoubleDQN}_t \equiv R_{t+1} + \gamma Q(S_{t+1}, \arg\max_a Q(S_{t+1}, a; \boldsymbol{\theta}_t), \boldsymbol{\theta}^-_t)$ — online network selects, target network evaluates.

nodes.name: Average value-estimate diagnostic
nodes.statement: $\frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \arg\max_a Q(S_t, a; \boldsymbol{\theta})$ over $T=125{,}000$ evaluation steps, used to compare estimated vs. true returns.

nodes.name: Normalized score
nodes.statement: $\text{score}_{\text{normalized}} = \dfrac{\text{score}_\text{agent} - \text{score}_\text{random}}{\text{score}_\text{human} - \text{score}_\text{random}}$.

nodes.name: Lower bound on Q-learning overestimation (Thrun-style tight bound)
nodes.statement: For state $s$ with $Q_*(s,a)=V_*(s)$ for all $a$, if estimates satisfy $\sum_a (Q_t(s,a)-V_*(s)) = 0$ and $\frac{1}{m}\sum_a (Q_t(s,a)-V_*(s))^2 = C > 0$ with $m \ge 2$, then $\max_a Q_t(s,a) \ge V_*(s) + \sqrt{C/(m-1)}$, and this lower bound is tight. Under the same conditions, the lower bound on the absolute error of the Double Q-learning estimate is zero.
nodes.statement_clean: Even with on-average-correct estimates, Q-learning's max is provably biased up by at least sqrt(C/(m-1)), while Double Q-learning admits a zero-error case.
assumptions: All true optimal action values equal: $Q_*(s,a) = V_*(s)$ for all $a$
conclusions: Lower bound on $|Q'_t(s, \arg\max_a Q_t(s,a)) - V_*(s)|$ is zero for Double Q-learning

nodes.name: Expected overoptimism under uniform errors
nodes.statement: If $Q_*(s,a) = V_*(s)$ for all $a$ and the estimation errors $Q_t(s,a) - Q_*(s,a)$ are i.i.d. uniform in $[-1,1]$, then $\mathbb{E}[\max_a Q_t(s,a) - V_*(s)] = \frac{m-1}{m+1}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (lower bound)
nodes.statement: By contradiction: assume $\max_a \epsilon_a < \sqrt{C/(m-1)}$. Split errors into $n$ positive and $m-n$ strictly negative parts; show $n \le m-1$, then bound $\sum_j (\epsilon^-_j)^2$ via H\"older's inequality and combine to obtain $\sum_a \epsilon_a^2 < mC$, contradicting the hypothesis. Tightness follows from the explicit construction $\epsilon_a = \sqrt{C/(m-1)}$ for $a < m$, $\epsilon_m = -\sqrt{(m-1)C}$. The Double Q-learning zero-error case is exhibited by an explicit configuration.

nodes.name: Contradiction setup
nodes.statement: Define $\epsilon_a = Q_t(s,a) - V_*(s)$ and assume for contradiction that $\max_a \epsilon_a < \sqrt{C/(m-1)}$.

nodes.name: Partition errors into positive and negative parts
nodes.statement: Let $\{\epsilon^+_i\}_{i=1}^n$ collect the strictly positive errors and $\{\epsilon^-_j\}_{j=1}^{m-n}$ the strictly negative ones. If $n=m$ then $\sum_a \epsilon_a = 0$ forces all $\epsilon_a = 0$, contradicting $\sum_a \epsilon_a^2 = mC$, so $n \le m-1$.

nodes.name: Bound positive sum and transfer to negatives
nodes.statement: $\sum_i \epsilon^+_i \le n \max_i \epsilon^+_i < n\sqrt{C/(m-1)}$. Using $\sum_a \epsilon_a = 0$, $\sum_j |\epsilon^-_j| < n\sqrt{C/(m-1)}$, hence $\max_j |\epsilon^-_j| < n\sqrt{C/(m-1)}$.

nodes.name: Apply H\"older's inequality on negative squares
nodes.statement: $\sum_j (\epsilon^-_j)^2 \le \sum_j |\epsilon^-_j| \cdot \max_j |\epsilon^-_j| < n\sqrt{C/(m-1)} \cdot n\sqrt{C/(m-1)}$.

nodes.name: Combine to derive contradiction
nodes.statement: $\sum_a \epsilon_a^2 = \sum_i (\epsilon^+_i)^2 + \sum_j (\epsilon^-_j)^2 < n\frac{C}{m-1} + n^2\frac{C}{m-1} = C\frac{n(n+1)}{m-1} \le mC$, contradicting $\sum_a \epsilon_a^2 = mC$.

nodes.name: Exhibit tight configuration
nodes.statement: Set $\epsilon_a = \sqrt{C/(m-1)}$ for $a=1,\ldots,m-1$ and $\epsilon_m = -\sqrt{(m-1)C}$; verify $\sum_a \epsilon_a = 0$ and $\sum_a \epsilon_a^2 = mC$, achieving equality in the bound.

nodes.name: Construct zero-error case for Double Q-learning
nodes.statement: Take $Q_t(s,a_1) = V_*(s) + \sqrt{C(m-1)/m}$, $Q_t(s,a_i) = V_*(s) - \sqrt{C/(m(m-1))}$ for $i>1$, and $Q'_t(s,a_1) = V_*(s)$; then $|Q'_t(s, \arg\max_a Q_t(s,a)) - V_*(s)| = 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2 (uniform-error expectation)
nodes.statement: Compute the CDF of $\max_a \epsilon_a$ via independence: $P(\max_a \epsilon_a \le x) = \prod_a P(\epsilon_a \le x) = ((1+x)/2)^m$ on $(-1,1)$. Differentiate to get density $f_{\max}(x) = \frac{m}{2}((1+x)/2)^{m-1}$ and integrate $\int_{-1}^1 x f_{\max}(x)\,dx = (m-1)/(m+1)$.

nodes.name: Reduce max-CDF to product via independence
nodes.statement: $P(\max_a \epsilon_a \le x) = \prod_{a=1}^m P(\epsilon_a \le x)$ since the $\epsilon_a$ are independent.

nodes.name: Identify uniform CDF
nodes.statement: $P(\epsilon_a \le x) = (1+x)/2$ on $(-1,1)$, $0$ below, $1$ above; hence $P(\max_a \epsilon_a \le x) = ((1+x)/2)^m$ on $(-1,1)$.

nodes.name: Differentiate to obtain density
nodes.statement: $f_{\max}(x) = \frac{d}{dx} P(\max_a \epsilon_a \le x) = \frac{m}{2}((1+x)/2)^{m-1}$ for $x \in [-1,1]$.

nodes.name: Evaluate the expectation integral
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}[\max_a \epsilon_a] = \int_{-1}^1 x f_{\max}(x)\,dx = \left[ ((x+1)/2)^m (mx-1)/(m+1) \right]_{-1}^1 = (m-1)/(m+1)$.

nodes.name: Q-learning
nodes.statement: Online TD update of action values using the bootstrap target $Y^Q_t = R_{t+1} + \gamma \max_a Q(S_{t+1},a;\boldsymbol{\theta}_t)$.

nodes.name: DQN (Deep Q-Network)
nodes.statement: Q-learning with deep neural network function approximation, a periodically-copied target network, and experience replay; bootstrap target is $Y^{DQN}_t$.

nodes.name: Double Q-learning
nodes.statement: Maintain two value functions $Q(\cdot;\boldsymbol{\theta})$ and $Q(\cdot;\boldsymbol{\theta}')$; on each update, use one to select the greedy action and the other to evaluate it, swapping roles randomly between updates.

nodes.name: Double DQN
nodes.statement: Minimal modification of DQN that decouples action selection from evaluation by selecting via the online network and evaluating via the target network: $Y^{DoubleDQN}_t = R_{t+1} + \gamma Q(S_{t+1}, \arg\max_a Q(S_{t+1},a;\boldsymbol{\theta}_t), \boldsymbol{\theta}^-_t)$.
output: Updated parameters $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ producing improved $Q$ estimates and policies

nodes.name: Select greedy action with online network
nodes.statement: Compute $a^* = \arg\max_a Q(S_{t+1}, a; \boldsymbol{\theta}_t)$ using the online network's current weights.

nodes.name: Evaluate selected action with target network
nodes.statement: Form target $Y^{DoubleDQN}_t = R_{t+1} + \gamma Q(S_{t+1}, a^*; \boldsymbol{\theta}^-_t)$ using the (frozen) target-network weights.

nodes.name: Online network gradient step
nodes.statement: Apply the standard DQN update $\boldsymbol{\theta}_{t+1} = \boldsymbol{\theta}_t + \alpha (Y^{DoubleDQN}_t - Q(S_t,A_t;\boldsymbol{\theta}_t)) \nabla_{\boldsymbol{\theta}_t} Q(S_t,A_t;\boldsymbol{\theta}_t)$ on a minibatch sampled from replay memory.

nodes.name: Periodic target-network refresh
nodes.statement: Every $\tau$ steps copy $\boldsymbol{\theta}^- \leftarrow \boldsymbol{\theta}$; otherwise hold $\boldsymbol{\theta}^-$ fixed.

nodes.name: Action-value overestimation in Q-learning with function approximation
nodes.statement: Determine whether overestimation of action values by Q-learning under function approximation is common in practice, whether it harms performance, and whether it can be mitigated at scale.

nodes.name: Polynomial-fit overestimation experiment (Figure 2)
nodes.statement: Continuous state $s$, 10 actions with identical true value $Q_*(s,a) = \sin(s)$ or $2 e^{-s^2}$; fit each action's value with a degree-$d$ polynomial ($d=6$ or $9$) on disjoint subsets of integer states. The max over actions is almost everywhere above the truth (orange curve), while the Double-Q estimator (blue) is much closer to zero — a fully deterministic illustration that estimation errors alone produce upward bias.

nodes.name: Standard-normal i.i.d. error bars (Figure 1)
nodes.statement: With $Q(s,a) = V_*(s) + \epsilon_a$ and $\epsilon_a \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$ i.i.d., the empirical bias of Q-learning grows with the number of actions $m$, while Double Q-learning is unbiased; averaged over 100 repetitions.

nodes.name: Atari overestimation curves (Figure 3)
nodes.statement: On six Atari 2600 games, DQN's running value-estimate $\frac{1}{T}\sum_t \arg\max_a Q(S_t,a;\boldsymbol{\theta})$ (orange) drifts substantially above the true discounted return of the learned policy (orange straight line); Double DQN curves (blue) track the true return closely, with markedly more stable learning. Asterix and Wizard of Wor show extreme DQN overestimation coinciding with score collapse.

nodes.name: No-op evaluation across 49 Atari games (Table 1)
nodes.statement: Under the no-op start protocol with $\epsilon$-greedy ($\epsilon=0.05$) over 100 episodes of 5-min play, normalized scores: DQN median $93.5\%$ / mean $241.1\%$ vs. Double DQN $114.7\%$ / $330.3\%$. Notable jumps include Road Runner ($233\%\to 617\%$), Asterix ($70\%\to 180\%$), Zaxxon ($54\%\to 111\%$), Double Dunk ($17\%\to 397\%$).

nodes.name: Human-starts robustness evaluation (Table 2)
nodes.statement: With 100 human-trajectory start states per game (30 min play): DQN $47.5\%/122.0\%$ (median/mean), Double DQN $88.4\%/273.1\%$, tuned Double DQN $116.7\%/475.2\%$. The tuned variant uses target-update period $\tau=30{,}000$, $\epsilon=0.01$ during training, $\epsilon=0.001$ at evaluation, and a shared output bias.

nodes.name: Lower bound is artifact of bound type, not typical behavior
nodes.statement: The lower bound in Theorem 1 decreases with $m$, but this is an artifact of requiring very specific configurations; typically, overoptimism increases with the number of actions, as illustrated in Figure 1.

nodes.name: Bootstrapping propagates overestimation
nodes.statement: Bootstrapping off already-overoptimistic action values propagates the bias and, because errors are state-action dependent rather than uniform, distorts the relative ordering of states and degrades the learned policy.

nodes.name: Distinction from optimism in the face of uncertainty
nodes.statement: These overestimations are not optimism in the face of uncertainty: they arise post-update as 'overoptimism in the face of apparent certainty', and (per Thrun & Schwartz 1993) impede rather than aid learning.

nodes.name: Double DQN as minimal modification to DQN
nodes.statement: Double DQN is the minimal change to DQN towards Double Q-learning: it reuses the existing target network as the second value function with no additional networks, parameters, or computational overhead.
